title: Strict boundary resolution of an excellent Noetherian log regular pair
statement:
Let $M$ be an integral excellent Noetherian scheme and $B\subset M$ a nowhere dense closed subset such that $(M,B)$ is a log regular pair. There exist an integral regular Noetherian scheme $R$, a proper birational morphism $e:R\to M$, and a strict normal crossings boundary $A\subset R$ such that $e^{-1}(B)\subseteq |A|$. Birational means inducing an isomorphism on dense open subschemes. At each point of $R$, on a sufficiently small neighbourhood, the distinct components of $A$ passing through that point have equations $t_1,\ldots,t_s$ which form part of a regular system of parameters; thus $A$ has local equation $t_1\cdots t_s=0$. The empty boundary is allowed.

The notions are [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-trf-log-regular-pair], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters].

source.place: Expose VII Theorem 4.3, printed pp. 82--83, followed by Expose VIII 4.1.2--4.1.8 (strictification), printed pp. 117--118, and Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118. Expose IX 2.4, printed p. 134, applies precisely this strict-boundary form to a general excellent log regular quotient.

proof.text: Put $U=M\setminus B$. It is a nonempty dense open since $M$ is integral and $B$ is nowhere dense. Give $M$ its divisorial fs log structure $\mathcal L$ from [def-trf-log-regular-pair]; its triviality locus is exactly $U$, and its log-regularity condition is the one in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. At a geometric point the characteristic monoid $P=\overline{\mathcal L}$ is sharp and saturated. Its group completion is torsion free: if $ng=0$, saturation puts both $g$ and $-g$ in $P$, so $g$ is a unit, hence zero by sharpness. The Noetherian scheme $M$ is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian. Thus [lem-trf-monoidal-resolution-tower] gives a finite saturated log blowup tower $(X_n,\mathcal L_n)\to\cdots\to(X_0,\mathcal L_0)=(M,\mathcal L)$ along nonempty coherent log ideals, with free final characteristic monoids. Write $b_i:X_{i+1}\to X_i$ for the underlying maps.

We will use the following chart observation at both stages. The blowup of a nonzero finite-type ideal $J$ on an integral scheme $X$ is integral. On an affine domain $A$, [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] gives the nonempty charts $\operatorname{Spec}A[J/a]$ for nonzero generators $a$. By [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], these are domains inside the same function field, each containing its generic point. The charts cover and share that point; the same is true across affine opens of $X$. Their union is reduced and irreducible, hence integral. Its normalization is integral as well: by [def-sc-normalization] its affine rings are integral closures of domains inside that same field, hence domains, again with a common generic point. A nonempty open on which the blowup or normalized blowup is an isomorphism is therefore dense in its source.

source.place: VIII 3.4.6(i), printed p. 111; explicit affine-chart argument, also Stacks 02ND (divisors.tex, lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme).

proof.text: Induct on $i$ with invariant: $X_i$ is integral excellent Noetherian, $(X_i,\mathcal L_i)$ is log regular, and its triviality locus $U_i$ is the inverse image of $U$ and maps isomorphically to $U$. The case $i=0$ is the hypothesis and Step 1. Given the invariant at $i$, [lem-trf-log-blowup-normalization] identifies $X_{i+1}$ with the normalization of $Y_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{J_i}X_i$, where $J_i$ is nonzero finite-type quasi-coherent; it gives log regularity and $U_{i+1}=b_i^{-1}U_i\cong U_i$. Step 2 makes both $Y_i$ and $X_{i+1}$ integral. By [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], $Y_i\to X_i$ is proper, hence finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $Y_i$ Noetherian.

source.place: VIII 3.4.5--3.4.9, printed pp. 111--112; ordinary blowup finiteness and Stacks 01T6 (morphisms.tex, lemma-finite-type-noetherian).

proof.text: Over an excellent affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X_i$, the finite-type definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] covers $Y_i$ by affine spectra of finite-type $A$-algebras. These rings are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. The affine-cover criterion [lem-trf-excellent-scheme-affine-cover] therefore makes $Y_i$ excellent. Apply [lem-per-excellent-normalization-preparation] to the integral, hence reduced, excellent Noetherian scheme $Y_i$. On an integral scheme its componentwise normalization is precisely normalization in its one function field, as in Step 2. Thus $X_{i+1}\to Y_i$ is finite and $X_{i+1}$ is excellent Noetherian. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] makes $b_i$ proper. This closes the induction of Step 3, including all the excellence hypotheses needed at the next stage.

source.place: VIII 3.4.6--3.4.9, printed pp. 111--112; Stacks 07QU (more-algebra.tex, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent), 0HAB (morphisms.tex, lemma-locally-excellent), 035S (lemma-nagata-normalization).

proof.text: Put $V=X_n$ and let $p:V\to M$ be the composite tower. Repeated application of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] makes $p$ proper; for a zero-length tower the identity is proper directly from [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The invariant gives $p^{-1}U\cong U$. By Step 1 the final characteristic monoids are free, so [lem-trf-free-characteristic-regular-boundary] makes $V$ regular and its reduced nontriviality locus $Z$ an effective Cartier normal crossings divisor. It also makes $p^{-1}U$ dense. Since the triviality locus is exactly $p^{-1}U$, the support of $Z$ is $p^{-1}B$. The scheme $V$ is integral excellent Noetherian by Steps 3--4. This proves the regular, possibly non-strict normal crossings stage without applying the existing finite-type-over-a-field resolution lemma.

source.place: VII Theorem 4.3, printed pp. 82--83; VIII 3.4.4, 3.4.8 and 4.1.1, printed pp. 110--111, 117.

proof.text: Set $V_0=V$, $B_0=D_0=Z$, $H_0=\varnothing$, and $q_0=1_V$. We now maintain: $V_j$ is integral regular Noetherian; $q_j:V_j\to V$ is proper and isomorphic over $V\setminus |Z|$; $B_j=(q_j^{-1}Z)_{\rm red}$ is normal crossings; $D_j$ is the remaining strict transform of $Z$ and a reduced union of components of $B_j$; $H_j$ is a strict normal crossings union of components of $B_j$; and $B_j=D_j\cup H_j$. These hold at $j=0$, with the empty boundary understood as the unit ideal. If $D_j$ is empty we stop. Otherwise [lem-trf-nc-maximal-branch-blowup] supplies a finite maximum branch number $m_j\ge1$ and its reduced regular closed locus $C_j$, with $C_j\subset D_j\subset B_j$ and, etale locally, $C_j=V(t_1,\ldots,t_{m_j})$, $D_j=V(t_1\cdots t_{m_j})$ in boundary parameters for $B_j$.

source.place: VIII 4.1.2--4.1.8, printed pp. 117--118: strict transform, accumulated exceptional boundary, and maximum-depth stratum.

proof.text: Blow up $C_j$: let $c_j:V_{j+1}\to V_j$ and $q_{j+1}=q_jc_j$. Its center ideal is finite type since $V_j$ is Noetherian, and is nonzero because it is the unit ideal on the nonempty open identified with $U$. By [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], $c_j$ is proper. It is an isomorphism off $C_j$ by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], hence over that open. Step 2 makes $V_{j+1}$ integral. Properness implies finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $V_{j+1}$ Noetherian. [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] makes $q_{j+1}$ proper. Thus the scheme, properness, and preserved-open parts of the invariant hold at the next stage.

source.place: VIII 4.1.2--4.1.4 and 4.1.8, printed pp. 117--118; Stacks 01T6 and the ordinary blowup-complement property.

proof.text: The center supplied in Step 6 is regular and is generated by a nonempty subset of the boundary parameters, exactly the center hypothesis of [lem-trf-permissible-boundary-preservation]. Apply it to $(V_j,B_j,H_j,C_j)$. It gives regular $V_{j+1}$, normal crossings $B_{j+1}=(c_j^{-1}B_j)_{\rm red}$, and strict normal crossings $H_{j+1}=(c_j^{-1}(H_j\cup C_j))_{\rm red}$, a union of components of $B_{j+1}$. With $E_{j+1}=(c_j^{-1}C_j)_{\rm red}$ it also gives $B_{j+1}=B_j^{\rm st}\cup E_{j+1}$ and $H_{j+1}=H_j^{\rm st}\cup E_{j+1}$. Meanwhile [lem-trf-nc-maximal-branch-blowup] gives that $D_{j+1}=D_j^{\rm st}$ is normal crossings or empty, and every one of its branch numbers is at most $m_j-1$.

The boundary identities also give $B_{j+1}=D_{j+1}\cup H_{j+1}$. Indeed strict transform is the scheme-theoretic closure away from the center [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Closure commutes with a finite scheme-theoretic union: on an affine chart its defining ideal is the kernel of restriction, and the kernel for a union is the intersection of the two kernels. Hence $B_j^{\rm st}=D_j^{\rm st}\cup H_j^{\rm st}$. Substitute the identities in Step 8. Reduction does not alter supports [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], so $B_{j+1}$ is also $(q_{j+1}^{-1}Z)_{\rm red}$. Since $D_{j+1}$ is normal crossings or empty and contained in $B_{j+1}$, its branches are a subset of the branches of $B_{j+1}$; thus it is again a reduced union of components. This completes the boundary part of the induction.

source.place: VIII 4.1.3--4.1.4(i) and 4.1.8, printed pp. 117--118; closure and reduced-union bookkeeping.

proof.text: If $Z$ is empty, take no blowups. Otherwise the positive integers $m_j$ strictly decrease whenever $D_j$ remains nonempty, by Step 8. Thus after at most $m_0$ steps $D_N=\varnothing$ and $B_N=H_N$. This includes $m_j=1$: the center is then all of $D_j$, possibly a Cartier center with identity blowup, but its strict transform is empty since $D_j\setminus C_j=\varnothing$. Put $R=V_N$, $q=q_N$ and $A=B_N=H_N$. By the invariant, $R$ is integral regular Noetherian, $q$ is proper and isomorphic over $V\setminus|Z|$, and $A$ is a strict normal crossings boundary with $|A|=q^{-1}|Z|$. The latter assertion has exactly the regular-component and intersection meaning of [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], supplied at every nonempty stage by [lem-trf-permissible-boundary-preservation].

source.place: VIII 4.1.6--4.1.8 and Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118; termination including the final Cartier center.

proof.text: We spell out the parameter clause, without interpreting etale normal crossings as strict normal crossings. At $x\in R$, discard the finitely many components of $A$ not containing $x$. In the regular local ring $(S,\mathfrak m)=\mathcal O_{R,x}$ of dimension $d$, let $I_1,\ldots,I_s$ be the ideals of the remaining distinct components. [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] gives that every $S/I_J$ for $I_J=\sum_{a\in J}I_a$ is regular local of dimension $d-|J|$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-independent-generators], $I_a$ has generators with independent images in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Its image there has dimension one: the quotient is the cotangent space of $S/I_a$, whose dimension is $d-1$, whereas that of $S$ is $d$, by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension]. Thus this independent generating set has exactly one member, say $I_a=(t_a)$.

source.place: VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118; Stacks 00NR (algebra.tex, lemma-regular-quotient-regular), with 00KU cotangent dimension.

proof.text: For $I=I_1+\cdots+I_s$, the same quotient-cotangent calculation gives $\dim_\kappa((I+\mathfrak m^2)/\mathfrak m^2)=d-(d-s)=s$. This space is spanned by the $s$ classes of $t_1,\ldots,t_s$, so they are independent. Extend them to a basis of $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ and lift the additional basis vectors to $\mathfrak m$. Nakayama in the generator form [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], applied to the finitely generated $S$-module $\mathfrak m$, says that the resulting $d$ elements generate $\mathfrak m$. Thus they are a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. By [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] the $t_a$ are pairwise nonassociate prime elements. Their principal ideals therefore have intersection $(t_1\cdots t_s)$: divisibility by each distinct prime implies divisibility by their product. The reduced union of the components has this ideal. Represent these finitely many germs on a common neighbourhood of $x$; equality of their finitely generated ideal stalks persists after shrinking. The component equations and product equation follow there. For $s=0$ the product is $1$ and the boundary is empty near $x$.

source.place: VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), printed p. 118; Stacks 00NR, 00KU (algebra.tex), and 0AG0 (more-algebra.tex, lemma-regular-local-UFD).

proof.text: Finally take $e=pq:R\to M$. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. The nonempty open $e^{-1}U$ is isomorphic to $U$ by the two preserved-open constructions, and is dense in the integral $R$; $U$ is dense in $M$. Thus $e$ is birational with precisely the dense-open meaning in the statement. From Step 5 and the boundary recurrence, $e^{-1}B=q^{-1}p^{-1}B=q^{-1}|Z|=|A|$ as closed supports, which in particular proves the requested containment. Regularity, integrality and Noetherianity were proved in the induction, and Steps 11--12 give every local parameter clause. If $B$ is empty all conclusions still apply, with $A$ empty.

source.place: VII Theorem 4.3, VIII 4.1.8 and IX 2.4, printed pp. 82--83, 118, 134.
